title: The Portrait of Ashcombe
premise: Wren Voss, coroner of the fog-bound town of Ashcombe, is paid a retainer by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder listed in an old church ledger has not yet occurred. The ledger, disguised as a century of burial records, encodes a pattern of deaths scheduled by date — and the next entry falls in nine days, bearing Wren's own name. As she traces the ledger's authorship to a vigilante circle of townsfolk who have been quietly executing unpunished crimes for generations, she must decide whether to expose them or join them. In the end, Wren fakes her own death to enter the circle from within, dismantles its leadership, and burns the ledger — choosing imperfect justice over both law and vengeance.
about_author: Ulyana Halloran is the pen name of a former rural records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing parish ledgers and small-town death registers before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the quiet violence hidden inside ordinary paperwork.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Wren Voss walks the Ashcombe cemetery at dawn, reciting names of the dead she has certified, establishing her pride and isolation. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: A pale stranger named Mr. Ellery pays Wren triple her fee to prove one thing: that the death recorded for March 14th in St. Brigid's ledger has not happened yet. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: unease masked as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Faithful
chapters.summary: In the church archive, Wren finds the burial ledger immaculate — too immaculate — with dates entered years ahead in faded ink. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: first true fear.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Wren decodes the first cipher layer: initials matching real, unsolved disappearances across decades. The March 14th entry reads 'W.V.' POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cold dread.

chapters.title: The Sheriff Who Smiles
chapters.summary: Wren tests Sheriff Dane Colm with a fabricated question; his easy deflection feels rehearsed. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: suspicion of everyone.

chapters.title: Ellery Vanishes
chapters.summary: Wren returns to Ellery's motel room: stripped bare, a single pressed violet left on the pillow — the same flower drawn beside each ledger entry. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: abandonment and resolve.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought
chapters.summary: A body washes up at Miller's Bend; Wren performs the autopsy and finds the man died two days ago yet was entered in the ledger eleven years ago. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: horror of precision.

chapters.title: The Violet Society
chapters.summary: Digging through town archives, Wren uncovers references to a 'Violet Circle' — founders' portraits where one face recurs across generations. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the town itself becomes suspect.

chapters.title: Mrs. Aldous Remembers
chapters.summary: An elderly widow hints that her husband 'was corrected' in 1974, then clams up when her son enters. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: complicity everywhere.

chapters.title: Correction
chapters.summary: Wren realizes the ledger isn't predicting murders — it's scheduling punishments for crimes the law failed to touch. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Her Own Cold Case
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the hit-and-run that killed Wren's sister, never solved, the reason she became a coroner. POV: Wren (past). Emotional beat: grief rekindled as motive.

chapters.title: Sister's Name in Ink
chapters.summary: Wren finds her sister's killer's initials in the ledger, marked 'corrected' the year after the crash — someone avenged her already. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: shattered certainty.

chapters.title: The Innkeeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Following paper trails, Wren reaches Harrow Inn, whose guestbook matches the ledger's handwriting across a century — one hand, unaging. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: uncanny pursuit.

chapters.title: Night at Harrow
chapters.summary: Wren stays the night; footsteps pass her door at 3 a.m., pausing, counting. She finds tally marks scratched inside the wardrobe. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: The Counting Man
chapters.summary: Wren glimpses the keeper, Tomas Reeve, who has run the inn for forty years looking exactly like photos from 1902. He warns her gently to stop. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: dread with pity.

chapters.title: Colm's File
chapters.summary: Wren breaks into the sheriff's office and finds Colm keeps his own copy of the ledger — he is a warden, not an enemy. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers
chapters.summary: Comparing copies, Wren sees entries added after printing: the Circle still meets, still chooses. The next name after hers is a child's. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: line crossed.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wren stakes out the child's family and discovers the father confessed privately to a crime the courts dismissed — the Circle has judged him through his daughter. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fury.

chapters.title: An Offer of Violets
chapters.summary: Tomas Reeve formally invites Wren to attend a Circle gathering, claiming she was always meant to be recruited, not killed. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: temptation.

chapters.title: The Gathering at the Chapel Below
chapters.summary: Beneath St. Brigid's crypt, twelve masked figures read judgments aloud. Wren attends veiled, hears her own case argued — her falsified autopsy reports protecting a mill owner. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: exposure of self.

chapters.title: Judged
chapters.summary: The Circle votes on Wren: her hypocrisy mirrors theirs. She is offered a chair instead of a grave. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: shame and dark belonging.

chapters.title: Chair Twelve
chapters.summary: Wren accepts provisionally, learning the rules: unanimous vote, violet proof, no children. But Chair Four keeps breaking rules. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: double life begins.

chapters.title: Chair Four
chapters.summary: Investigating internally, Wren identifies Chair Four as Sheriff Colm, who has been adding personal enemies to the ledger. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: The Mill Owner's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren confronts the mill owner whose crimes she once buried; he confesses on tape, giving her leverage and guilt in equal measure. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: costly truth.

chapters.title: March 13th
chapters.summary: One day before her scheduled death, Wren stages evidence of her own murder — a body, her blood, a closed casket. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: calculated self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Funeral of Wren Voss
chapters.summary: The town buries her; Wren watches from the bell tower, unseen, feeling the strange freedom and cost of being dead. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: elegy for herself.

chapters.title: What Colm Buried
chapters.summary: Free of her identity, Wren raids Colm's private records and finds he murdered Ellery — the stranger who hired her was trying to stop the Circle from within. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief for an ally.

chapters.title: Reeve's Century
chapters.summary: Tomas Reeve confesses the truth: he is the third keeper of a system begun as protection for mill girls in 1898, now rotted into habit. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: tragic inheritance.

chapters.title: The Vote on the Child
chapters.summary: The Circle convenes to judge the ferryman through his daughter; Wren must vote. She casts the sole dissent — and reveals Colm's forged entries. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: open rebellion.

chapters.title: Chairs Turned
chapters.summary: Colm accuses Wren of faking her death; half the Circle turns on her. She flees the crypt through the ossuary tunnels as chairs overturn behind her. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: flight.

chapters.title: Tunnels of the Named
chapters.summary: Lost beneath Ashcombe among bones tagged with ledger names, Wren realizes every 'corrected' victim rests here, unmourned. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: witness to the buried.

chapters.title: Colm at the Door
chapters.summary: Cornered, Wren fights Colm in the bone gallery; she wins by refusing to kill him, forcing the observing Circle members to see the difference between justice and murder. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: mercy as weapon.

chapters.title: The Unanimity Breaks
chapters.summary: Shaken, three chairs side with Wren; Reeve casts the deciding voice against Colm, invoking the founding rule: no punishment without unanimity. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the system devours its corruptor.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Ledger
chapters.summary: By unanimous new vote, the Circle burns the ledger in the crypt; Wren insists the tunnel bones be named and buried properly first. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: mourning made public.

chapters.title: Resurrection Papers
chapters.summary: Wren negotiates her return: Reeve's confession, sealed, buys her legal resurrection; the town accepts a story about mistaken identity. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: uneasy amnesty.

chapters.title: The Grave That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Wren exhumes the casket she filled and gives the unnamed body — a Circle victim from decades past — a real funeral with a real name. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: restitution.

chapters.title: Colm's Cell
chapters.summary: Visiting Colm in county jail, Wren refuses his claim that they are the same; she leaves him the pressed violet from Ellery's room. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: closure without absolution.

chapters.title: New Entries
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Wren opens a fresh notebook and writes only the names of the dead needing witness — no dates ahead, no judgments pending. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: vocation remade.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Grave
chapters.summary: Wren buries Ellery under his true name, researched at last, and speaks the eulogy she couldn't give her sister. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief finally spoken.

chapters.title: Portrait of Ashcombe
chapters.summary: Standing before the founders' portrait, Wren adds nothing and removes nothing — but hangs beside it a photograph of every named bone from the tunnel. The town looks, and does not look away. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: belonging earned, price acknowledged.
